You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
This looks like mid-2019. The fed funds rate is 2.39%, which fits the period before the July 2019 cut. The 10-year yield at 2.06% and the 2-year at 1.85% match June 2019, and unemployment of 3.7% and core CPI of 2.13% fit as well.

Several other readings point the same way. US large-cap equity is up 12.2% over 6 months, gold is up 10.6% over 3 months, and the 7-10y Treasury return of 4.4% over 3 months fits a falling-yield period. The 10-year yield had fallen 0.45 over 3 months, from about 2.5% in March to about 2.0% in June.

Month-end June 2019 fits best. The 1-month equity return of +0.6% looks low for June 2019, when the S&P gained about 7%. May 2019 returned about -6%, so neither month matches cleanly. The 3-month equity return of 2.4% would instead fit a different month-end.

Checking July 2019: the S&P returned about +1.4%, and the fed funds rate was 2.40 in July. The 10-year yield at the end of July was 2.01%, and the 2-year was 1.88%. The 3-month equity return of about 2.4% (May -6.3%, June +7%, July +1.4%) works out to roughly +1.5%, which is close. For July, developed ex-US fell about 1.5-2%, and gold was up about 0.5%. Gold rose about 8% in June, so +2.0% for 1 month does not fit well for either month.

August 2019 is another option. The 10-year yield ended August at 1.50%, which is too low. That leaves July or June, and the fed funds rate of 2.39 suits July (June was also 2.38). The 3-month change in the policy rate of -0.06 suggests a rate that had edged down, which fits June or July. I'll go with July.
